nodes.statement: U01 Study 4 analyzes 72 novice participants across six language conditions; Ruby, Python and Quorum outperform Randomo on token accuracy, while Java and Perl do not show a significant advantage over Randomo. Most real-language pairwise differences are not significant.
limitations: Novice short tasks; token accuracy; language-feature bundles; a non-significant contrast is not equivalence.

nodes.statement: Adapt familiar declaration forms for a defined audience, while testing semantic interpretation independently of punctuation.
limitations: Neither paper evaluates TypeScript or finance developers.
nodes.proposed_test: Compare semantically equivalent financial clauses, stratifying by prior TypeScript and functional-language experience.

nodes.statement: U01 intuition surveys had 166 respondents each with some overlap; generic-syntax ratings were inconclusive.
limitations: Ratings are not task performance; self-reported experience.

nodes.statement: U02 Auction correct completion was 7/10 Obsidian versus 2/10 Solidity. The p≈0.015 comparison conditions on claimed completion; the all-participant comparison was p≈0.070.
limitations: 20 analyzed Java programmers; one long-tutorial participant excluded; short training and task.

nodes.statement: In U02 Casino, all four Obsidian participants with compiling completed programs misused disown; none had a fully correct solution. One Solidity participant had a fully correct solution.
limitations: Variable remaining task time; difficult task; one compiler-bug case discarded; not a population effect estimate.

nodes.statement: Defer general unchecked escape hatches; evaluate whether repair attempts discard obligations or assets to silence diagnostics.
limitations: Moriarty is not Obsidian; scoped language semantics require separate design justification.
nodes.proposed_test: Observe seeded residual-duty and asset-loss repairs, including requests for unchecked casts or suppressed checks.

nodes.statement: U04 retained 27 of 33 recruited students. Static typing favored three API tasks and dynamic typing two; the task-specific analysis does not establish a universal type-system winner.
limitations: Java-familiar students; carryover; exclusions; stripped-static Groovy API; no mainstream IDE feature comparison.

nodes.statement: Adapt explicit type information at public financial boundaries and study inferred locals separately from erasing types.
limitations: Annotations and checking are confounded in this study; inference was future work.
nodes.proposed_test: Equal-signature explicit-local versus inferred-local condition with type display; measure navigation, mistakes and repair time.

nodes.statement: U05 message quizzes had 27 complete cases: incorrect interpretation was 17.28% for standard messages and 6.17% for enhanced messages, with reported paired-test p<0.035.
limitations: Message comprehension outside programming context; does not estimate secure repair.

nodes.statement: U05 think-aloud programming study did not show a substantial overall learning-outcome improvement, despite observations of useful reading and edits in response to enhanced messages.
limitations: 31 sessions; historical semester comparison; compiler access, prior-code access and teacher differences.

nodes.statement: Adopt separate measures of diagnostic comprehension, correct repair, recurrence and suppression attempts.
limitations: Friendly wording alone is not a demonstrated productivity intervention.
nodes.proposed_test: Seed wrong-asset, recipient, fee and rounding errors; measure first edit and eventual correct obligation-preserving repair.

nodes.statement: U06 Table 4 reports DSL/GPL success means of 57.62/40.95 learning, 64.57/50.86 perceiving, 70.95/33.33 evolving, and 64.34/43.37 overall, in percent.
limitations: 35 retained students; GUI questionnaire comparison, not production coding.

nodes.statement: U06 conclusion summarizes roughly 15% improvement across categories; Table 4 instead gives 16.67, 13.71 and 37.62 percentage-point differences, and 20.97 overall. Use explicit table numbers.
limitations: No raw-data reanalysis; publisher discrepancy preserved.

nodes.statement: U06 inferential statistics require caution: its prose calls the test independent although participants answered both questionnaires; cognitive-dimension attribution assumes equal contribution among selected dimensions.
limitations: This is a methodological limitation identified from the paper, not a reanalysis or disproof of its directional observation.

nodes.statement: Adapt domain-specific financial vocabulary, but defer importing the GUI study effect size into finance.
limitations: One domain and two specific notations; prior familiarity uneven.
nodes.proposed_test: Compare equivalent partial-payment and rounding-policy edits; include duty survival and wrong-recipient detection.

nodes.statement: U09 pilot uses 18 respondents: ten unsupervised and eight interviewed. Respondents identify concrete usability issues, but group, questionnaire and interview differences prevent a clean causal comparison.
limitations: Small convenience pilot, no validated scalar language ranking.

nodes.statement: Adopt cognitive-dimension prompts for visibility, dependencies, change effort and role clarity; defer a summed score ranking entire languages.
limitations: Usability concerns notation plus environment.
nodes.proposed_test: Ask reviewers to locate all clauses affected by an asset-unit, rounding-policy or residual-duty change.

nodes.statement: U10 reports eight student designers and six completed projects; spontaneous syntax choices and actual task failures reveal prior-experience effects and mistaken designer assumptions.
limitations: Qualitative convenience studies; end-user counts not consistently specified; no final-language performance trial.

nodes.statement: Adapt natural-programming tasks as formative evidence, followed by trained tasks on the actual constrained semantics.
limitations: Spontaneously invented syntax is not proof of learnability or safety.
nodes.proposed_test: Elicit an asset-bound limit, partial repayment and delayed claim before teaching spelling; then test interpretation and repair.

nodes.statement: Do content-addressed definitions and explicit dependency identity improve financial-language maintenance compared with name/version-oriented modules?
limitations: None of these seven works directly evaluates Unison or content addressing.
nodes.proposed_test: Compare rename and dependency-update tasks with equivalent semantic checks; track mistaken assumptions about what changed.

nodes.statement: U02 describes both Glacier programming-task contrasts as significant, but one reported p≈0.077 exceeds the conventional 0.05 threshold; retain counts and precise p-values.
limitations: No reanalysis; do not call this contrast significant at 0.05.

nodes.statement: Positive bounded-task results and negative open-ended outcomes can coexist; language evaluations should preserve correctness, completion and time as distinct outcomes.
limitations: Heterogeneous tasks and populations; no pooled effect estimate warranted.

nodes.statement: FElm separates normalization of functional expressions from ongoing signal execution. Its stratified types exclude signals of signals. Theorem 1 establishes type soundness and normalization of the first stage. The pipelined signal semantics uses unbounded FIFO queues; async preserves order inside a subgraph while relaxing global order between subgraphs. The implementation section explicitly omits direct performance evaluations.
Use immutable state transitions and explicitly identified inputs for tooling. Keep async results as proposals until authority and ledger checks accept them.
Neither first-stage normalization nor responsiveness establishes finite lifetime execution, finite queues, observation truth, quantitative conservation, or ledger acceptance.

Simply RaTT uses later and stable modalities with context restrictions, guarded recursion and a two-heap machine. For closed well-typed streams over value types built from unit, Nat, sums and products, Theorem 3.1 gives arbitrarily long finite productive prefixes. Theorem 3.2 gives typed stream-transducer progress; its proof establishes causality. The machine can discard the previous heap. The type system rejects a particular fixed-point-under-delay time leak.
Treat temporal availability as an independent typing concern. Define a bounded observation record with identity, effective time, expiry and authority before considering reactive syntax.

Productivity describes potentially infinite execution. Garbage collection does not establish a uniform byte/time bound; explicit state can grow. Fairness extensions are future work. These results say nothing about financial liveness or mandatory proofs.

nodes.source_locator: Overview/Nix Store pp.81–83; Implementation/The Store and Building Components pp.84–85; User Environment Policies pp.87–88; Conclusion p.91 (PDF pages subtract 78)
nodes.statement: Nix separates user-facing names from immutable installation objects, identifies variants through hashes of build inputs, lowers high-level expressions to simpler store expressions, and deploys dependency closures. Build inputs include scripts, platform and environment bindings. The paper describes atomic environment changes through POSIX rename and retains old generations. Mutable service state is explicitly outside Nix control.

nodes.source_locator: Overview/Nix Store pp.81–83; Implementation/The Store and Building Components pp.84–85; User Environment Policies pp.87–88; Conclusion p.91 (PDF pages subtract 78)
nodes.statement: Use separate source, Core, build and output identities. Include semantic profile, dependency closure and toolchain in artifact manifests. Authorize mutable financial migration separately from changing a code name.

nodes.source_locator: Overview/Nix Store pp.81–83; Implementation/The Store and Building Components pp.84–85; User Environment Policies pp.87–88; Conclusion p.91 (PDF pages subtract 78)
nodes.statement: An input-derived identifier assumes adequately captured inputs and appropriate determinism. It is not an independently checked output digest, semantic-equivalence proof, authorization, or migration theorem. The paper’s old hash examples are historical, not a recommended modern construction.

Koka uses strict evaluation and inferred row-polymorphic effects with duplicate labels. In its formal calculus, absence of exn excludes an unhandled exception result, not internally caught exceptions; absence of div entails termination. Heap encapsulation prevents local references escaping under its typing side conditions. The formal read primitive conservatively includes divergence; §2.7 distinguishes a finer implementation analysis and an incompletely implemented constraint case.

Give Moriarty primitive effects explicit typing and operational rules; close admitted effect sets before execution. Keep effect summaries separate from authority quantities and ordered ledger effects.

Termination alone does not give a registered work bound. Effect rows are not payment counts, rights, or affine continuation rules. This 2014 source does not establish the behavior of current Koka or arbitrary user-defined handlers.

The framework separates scheduling from rebuilding. Correctness preserves reachable inputs and requires every reachable computed key to agree with recomputation against the final store, assuming acyclic tasks. Verifying traces store hashes; constructive traces also store results. Deep traces omit intermediate dependencies and require determinism. The §6.4 Frankenbuild example combines nondeterministic intermediates with deep caching to yield inconsistent artifacts.

Cache each proof/compile stage by its actual immediate inputs and output identity; record semantic/compiler changes as dependencies. Specify an invalidation test for changed profile, kernel, observation policy and verifier lineage.

These are simplified executable models, not a certification of contemporary build products. Correct build outputs need not implement correct financial semantics. Shallow storage and nondeterminism change the correctness predicate.

nodes.source_locator: Ch.3 pp.13–21; Ch.4 pp.22–31; Ch.6 pp.39–40; Ch.7 p.41 (PDF pages add 3)
nodes.statement: The thesis explains discrete signals, lift and foldp, a two-tier intermediate representation, and explicit async subgraphs. Let-bound signal representations prevent duplicate runtime nodes. Its examples separate presentation from reactive processing. Chapter 6 records concrete JavaScript backend limitations; Chapter 7 presents filtering and further reactive machinery as future work.

nodes.source_locator: Ch.3 pp.13–21; Ch.4 pp.22–31; Ch.6 pp.39–40; Ch.7 p.41 (PDF pages add 3)
nodes.statement: Prefer an approachable functional surface over a small explicit Core, with stable diagnostic/source mappings. Keep preview recomputation separate from accepted state and residual obligations.

nodes.source_locator: Ch.3 pp.13–21; Ch.4 pp.22–31; Ch.6 pp.39–40; Ch.7 p.41 (PDF pages add 3)
nodes.statement: Historical syntax and runtime claims do not specify current Elm. The thesis and PLDI paper belong to the same research line, so they are not independent replications. Embedding/dynamic-switching discussion does not authorize dynamic or unbounded financial execution.
Current Elm architecture uses Model/View/Update with commands/subscriptions; the May2016 Elm0.17 post replaces signals. Historical FRP papers do not specify current Elm.
